description:
FILED s543b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16) while probing #5082's openers.  PRE-EXISTING (base c5f618f2 = the same).  LOUD: PCL dies where perl works, in ordinary code.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | PCL main c5f618f2):
    my $r; my $w; pipe $r, $w or die "pipe"; print $w "x\n"; close $w; print scalar <$r>;
    # perl: x     PCL: dies "Can't use an undefined value as filehandle reference"
    use Socket; my $a1; my $b1; socketpair($a1, $b1, AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, PF_UNSPEC) or die; print "ok\n";
    # perl: ok    PCL: the same death
`my ($r, $w); pipe($r, $w)` (one list declaration) and `pipe my $r, my $w` WORK -- only a second handle variable declared in a statement of its own.

EMISSION: `(p-let (($r :box (make-p-box nil))) (p-let (($w :scalar (p-undef))) (p-or (p-pipe $r $w) ...)))` -- $w is a RAW slot, so p-pipe's install arg receives the undef keyword and %p-fh-place-check dies (rule 12's undef guard, correctly).

CAUSE: Pl/VarAnnotator.pm `_tw_walk`: "handle-viv/tie/pos/4-arg-substr write only their FIRST argument" -- true for open/opendir/sysopen/socket/accept, FALSE for `pipe` (READHANDLE, WRITEHANDLE) and `socketpair` (SOCKET1, SOCKET2), which vivify their first TWO.  The text-scan twin (the `handle-viv-arg` regex near line 561) has the same first-argument-only reading, and `arg_writing_builtin` (shared with Parser2's #189 writes_args) is the third reader of the same table.

FIX DIRECTION: the handle-viv table carries how many leading arguments the builtin vivifies (pipe 2, socketpair 2, the rest 1); `_tw_walk` marks those; the text scan's regex learns the second slot for the two names.  Emission changes for every program with this shape (corpus-diff).  Guard: a row in Pl/t/handle-place-01.t or open-modes-01.t (perl oracle), both declaration spellings.
subject: LOUD: `my $r; my $w; pipe $r, $w` (and socketpair) dies "Can't use an undefined value as filehandle reference" -- the SECOND handle variable, declared in its own statement, is a raw slot (VarAnnotator marks only the first argument)
